task.description: Produce a backend design artefact for OBS-06 at src/design/obs-06-alerting-hooks.md. Define a configurable alerting-hook architecture for webhook notifications on three triggers: (1) instance stuck in ERROR for > N minutes, (2) DLQ depth threshold crossing, and (3) scheduler lag threshold breach. Specify configuration schema (enabled hooks, thresholds, destination URL, auth headers/secrets handling, retry policy) and clear state-machine semantics for one-shot threshold crossing behavior (fire once above threshold, re-arm only after recovery below threshold). Define payload contracts per alert type with deterministic fields and correlation IDs. Design delivery guarantees and failure handling: 3 retries with exponential backoff, structured logging on terminal failure (OBS-01), and no unbounded retry loops. Include module boundaries, data flows, idempotency safeguards, and integration points with OBS-05, SCH-02, and EXT-02. Provide a full requirement traceability matrix mapping all OBS-06 acceptance criteria and edge cases to concrete modules/functions plus test obligations. Design only; do not modify implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: All OBS-06 acceptance criteria and edge cases map to explicit design elements
Alert trigger semantics are concrete for ERROR duration, DLQ threshold crossing/re-arm, and scheduler lag
Webhook payload and configuration contracts are specified with security handling and deterministic fields
Retry/backoff and terminal-failure logging behavior are testable and aligned with OBS-01
Traceability matrix identifies implementation modules and verification hooks for backend and integration tests

result.summary: Design artefact for OBS-06 alerting hooks completed at src/design/obs-06-alerting-hooks.md, including configurable hook schema, one-shot threshold crossing and re-arm semantics for ERROR/DLQ/scheduler lag triggers, deterministic payload contracts with correlation IDs, bounded retry/backoff and OBS-01 terminal logging behavior, idempotency safeguards, and complete requirement traceability.
